title: Teriyaki Chicken
subtitle: Grilled chicken thighs with a sticky soy and mirin glaze
excerpt: Teriyaki chicken is Japanese grilled chicken coated in a sweet and salty soy, mirin, and sake glaze. The glaze is applied in stages during cooking, building up to a lacquered, sticky coating. Boneless chicken thighs give the best result: they stay juicy and caramelise well.
sourceNotes: Teriyaki (teri: shine, yaki: grill or broil) is a Japanese cooking method in which food is glazed with soy sauce and mirin during grilling. The technique dates to the 17th century. In the UK it is primarily known as a chicken dish; in Japan it also applies to fish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The marinade can be made up to 3 days ahead. Marinate the chicken overnight for a deeper flavour.

content.text: Teriyaki chicken is one of the most useful Japanese recipes to have in your repertoire. The method is simple: marinate the chicken, sear it skin-side down in a dry pan until the fat renders and the skin crisps, then baste with the glaze as you finish it in the oven. The glaze reduces onto the chicken surface in a deep, sticky lacquer.

Mix together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger, and garlic in a bowl. Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to overnight in the fridge. Reserve any leftover marinade.
Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Lift the chicken from the marinade, letting the excess drip off. Pour the reserved marinade into a small saucepan and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until syrupy. Set aside.
Heat an ovenproof frying pan over medium-high heat. No oil needed. Place the chicken skin-side down and cook without moving for 5 to 6 minutes until deep golden and much of the fat has rendered out.

Flip the chicken. Brush the top with reduced glaze. Transfer the pan to the oven and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through. Brush with more glaze halfway through. Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Scatter with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.

items.cause: Heat too high or glaze applied too early
items.fix: Apply the glaze only in the last 5 minutes of cooking. The sugar content means it burns quickly at very high heat.

items.symptom: Chicken is not cooked through after the stated time
items.cause: Thighs were unusually thick or the pan was too cold when the chicken went in
items.fix: Return to the oven for 3 to 4 minutes at a time, checking with an instant-read thermometer. Target: 75°C in the thickest part.

content.text: Serve over plain steamed rice with a green vegetable alongside: tenderstem broccoli, pak choi, or edamame. The sweet-salty glaze works with anything neutral.
